note: COMPUTED FROM THE AUTHORS' PUBLISHED EFFECT-SIZE ARCHIVE, not read off the figure. Source: Awad, Dsouza, Kim, Schulz, Henrich, Shariff, Bonnefon & Rahwan (2018), 'The Moral Machine experiment', Nature 563:59-64, doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0637-6; OSF project osf.io/3hvt2, file Datasets/Moral Machine Effect Sizes/plotdatamain.rdata - the source data for Figure 2a (n = 35.2 million decisions). The archive gives the nine global AMCEs (delta-P) with standard errors: Species 0.582736 (0.000947), No. Characters 0.508132 (0.000662), Age 0.490328 (0.000788), Law 0.351348 (0.000925), Social Status 0.345112 (0.001504), Fitness 0.160909 (0.000590), Gender 0.116780 (0.000667), Relation to AV 0.096815 (0.000653), Intervention 0.060556 (0.000355). The mapping from estimates to attributes is fixed by the file itself: the RData carries the Label factor codes [9,8,4,7,6,5,3,2,1] alongside the estimates, indexing the level list Species / No. Characters / Age / Law / Social Status / Fitness / Gender / Relation to AV / Intervention. It is confirmed independently by the Fig. 2 caption, which states the Age effect as 0.49 against the file's 0.490328. The extracted table is stored as scoring/human_baselines/sources/awad_2018_moral_machine_amce_fig2a.csv next to the original RData. (An earlier version of this note paired four of the standard errors with the wrong attributes; the estimates, which are what the baselines use, were unaffected.) delta-P is defined in the caption as 'the difference between the probability of sparing characters possessing the attribute on the right, and the probability of sparing characters possessing the attribute on the left'. A dilemma is binary, so the two probabilities sum to 1 and p = (1 + delta-P) / 2. Intervention is signed negatively because the reported preference is for INACTION, giving P(choose action) = (1 - 0.060556) / 2 = 0.470. SUPERSEDES prop_save_human 0.85 -> 0.791, prop_utilitarian 0.77 -> 0.754, prop_save_legal 0.61 -> 0.676, prop_intervention 0.46 -> 0.470. prop_save_young was already 0.745 from the caption and the archive confirms it to four decimal places. human_sd IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN FROM THIS ARCHIVE. The reported standard errors are ~0.001 because n is 35.2 million; they describe the precision of the population estimate, not between-person variation. Using them as the z-score denominator would make any deviation from the human mean a z of hundreds. The existing sds (0.10-0.13) are retained as between-person estimates and remain the one unsourced element of this task. ONE DESIGN NOTE: the Fig. 2 caption reports the number-of-characters effect separately for one to four additional characters, and states that the two-additional-character effect matches the attribute mean. The attribute mean is used here, so prop_utilitarian is exact only if this port shows two additional characters on average.
